title: Learning from label proportions for a visual matrix speller (ERP)
description: EEG recordings from 13 healthy participants performing an online copy-spelling task with a visual 6x7 matrix ERP speller. The speller was designed for learning from label proportions (LLP), an unsupervised, calibrationless classification approach for ERP-based brain-computer interfaces. Two stimulus sequences with different target/non-target ratios allowed the classifier to reconstruct mean target and non-target responses without labeled data. In the original study, 84.5% of characters were spelled correctly on average without prior calibration.
methods_description: Participants copy-spelled a German pangram three times using a 6x7 visual matrix speller with 250 ms SOA and salient highlighting. Each character comprised 68 highlighting events (4 sequences of 8 stimuli and 2 sequences of 18). EEG was recorded with a BrainAmp DC amplifier and 31 passive Ag/AgCl electrodes at 1000 Hz, with a nose reference and FCz ground. EOG, pulse and respiration were recorded as auxiliary channels. The LLP classifier was reset at the start of each sentence and retrained after each character.
